And whether We show you (some of) what We have promised them, or We take you (in death) before that, your duty is only to convey the message, and the reckoning is upon Us, not upon you: their accounting and their recompense for their deeds. So let not their turning away concern you, and do not hasten their punishment.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 13, verse 41:

﴿Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts?﴾ The land of disbelief (arḍ al-kufr), reduced from its extremities by what We open to the Muslims from their lands. So the abode of war (dār al-ḥarb) diminishes and the abode of Islam (dār al-Islām) increases, and this is among the signs of victory and triumph, and the like. ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? Are they then the victors?﴾ ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons﴾. The meaning: upon you is only the delivery (al-balāgh) of what you were charged with; do not be distressed by what lies beyond that, for We will suffice you for it and complete what We have promised you of triumph. Let not its delay weary you, for that is due to the interests (maṣāliḥ) that We know and you do not know. Then He consoles his heart and soothes his soul by mentioning the first signs of victory (tabāshīr al-ẓafar).

It is also read: *nanquṣuhā* (with intensive doubling of the qāf), meaning the same.

﴿There is none to repel His decree﴾: there is none to reject His judgment. The *muʿaqqib* is one who returns upon a thing and nullifies it. Its real sense is one who follows it up (yuʿqibuhu), i.e., pursues it with rejection and annulment. From this it is said of the rightful claimant: *muʿaqqib*, because he pursues his debtor with demand and claim. Labīd said:

*"The pursuit of the muʿaqqib, the wronged one, for his right"*[[*Until, in the midday heat, he hastens her... the pursuit of the muʿaqqib, the wronged one, for his right*

This is by Labīd ibn Rabīʿa, describing a wild ass that went out in the noon heat behind its she-ass. *Wa-hājahā*: he urged her on and spurred her to swift movement in pursuing her, just as the wronged muʿaqqib pursues his right and his debt from the one who owes it. So *al-maẓlūm* in the nominative is an epithet of *al-muʿaqqib*, since it is the grammatical subject in meaning.

Its meaning is one who returns to his right which he had given as a debt, as if he returned upon his heels, or because he follows and pursues the debtor.]]

The meaning: He has decreed for Islam victory and advance, and against disbelief retreat and reversal. ﴿And He is swift in reckoning﴾: so before long He will call them to account in the Hereafter after the punishment of this world. If you ask: what is the place (maḥall) of His saying ﴿there is none to repel His decree﴾? I say: it is a clause in a place of accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), as if it were said: "And Allah judges, His judgment being executed," just as you say, "Zayd came to me without a turban on his head or a cap," meaning "bareheaded."

And those before them did plot, but to Allah belongs all plotting. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the ultimate abode.

[Translation of the commentary:]

He described them as plotters, then made their plotting as nothing (kull makr) in comparison to His plotting, so He said: ﴿To Allah belongs all plotting﴾. Then He explained that with His saying: ﴿He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the ultimate abode﴾, because whoever knows what every soul earns and prepares for it its recompense, then the plotting is all His, for it comes upon them from where they do not perceive. And they are heedless of what is intended for them.

It is also read: "al-Kuffar" (the disbelievers), "al-Kafirun" (the disbelievers), "alladhina kafaru" (those who disbelieved), and "al-Kufr" (disbelief):

i.e., its people, and what is meant by "al-kafir" is the category. And Jinah ibn Habish read: "wa-sa-ya'lamu al-kafiru" (and the disbeliever will know), from a'lamahu, i.e., he will inform.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 13, verse 43:

﴿God suffices as a witness between me and you﴾, for what He has manifested of the proofs of my prophethood, ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾. The one who has knowledge of the Qur'an [[Mahmud said: "The intended meaning is: 'and the one who has knowledge of the Qur'an…' etc." Ahmad said: Then the intended meaning would be: the category of believers.]] and what it was composed upon of the miraculous arrangement, which surpasses the capacities of human beings. And it is said: he who is one of the scholars of the People of the Book [[Mahmud said: "And it is said: he who is one of the scholars of the People of the Book who embraced Islam, because they bear witness to his description in their scriptures." Ahmad said: So "the Book" in the first interpretation refers specifically to the Qur'an, and in the second to the category of the earlier books that preceded it.]] who have embraced Islam, because they bear witness to his description in their scriptures. And it is said: it is God, Exalted and Majestic [[Mahmud said: "And it is said: it is God, Exalted and Majestic, and 'the Book' is the Preserved Tablet. It is related from al-Hasan: 'No, by God, it means only God.' The meaning: 'God suffices as a witness, He who deserves worship and He who alone knows what is in the Preserved Tablet, as a witness between me and you.' And it is supported by the reading of those who read 'and whoever has knowledge of the Book' with 'man' as a preposition." Ahmad said: Al-Zamakhshari estimated the name of God in the coordinated element as "He who deserves worship," to avoid conjoining an attribute to what it qualifies, and moving to the view that he coordinated one of the two attributes with the other by estimation. He derived the restriction from his saying "and none knows the knowledge of the Book except Him," from his placing the predicate, which is "with Him," before its subject. It is characteristic of al-Zamakhshari to derive restriction from fronting. And God is the Granter of success to the truth.]] and "the Book" is the Preserved Tablet. It is related from al-Hasan: "No, by God, it means only God." The meaning: "God suffices as a witness, He who deserves worship and He who alone knows the knowledge of what is in the Tablet, as a witness between me and you." It is supported by the reading of those who read "and whoever has knowledge of the Book," with "man" as a preposition, i.e., "and from whose presence is the knowledge of the Book," because the knowledge of whoever possesses it is from His grace and kindness. It is also read: "and whoever has knowledge of the Book" with "man" as a preposition, and "ʿilm" in the passive form. It is also read: "and by whoever has knowledge of the Book."

If you say: by what is "ʿilm al-kitāb" in the nominative? I say: in the reading in which "ʿinda" is a relative clause (ṣila), "al-ʿilm" is nominative by the implied element within the adverbial phrase, so it becomes the subject, because when an adverbial phrase falls as a relative clause it intensifies its resemblance to a verb by relying on the relative pronoun, so it works as a verb does, as when you say: "I passed by the one who is in the house, whose brother…," so "akhūhu" is the subject, just as you say: "by the one who settled in the house, his brother." In the reading in which "ʿinda" is not a relative clause, "al-ʿilm" is nominative by the inchoative.

It is related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Ra'd will be given the reward of ten good deeds for the weight of every cloud that has passed and every cloud that will occur until the Day of Resurrection, and he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection among those who fulfill the covenant of God [[Its chain of narration has been mentioned earlier in Al ʿImran.]].
